parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, documented border targeting, facility ban, or state custody abuse is documented, and decriminalisation in 2022 was followed by reported safer feelings, long-running large Pride, operating bars and youth acceptance. Against that, there is no gender-identity anti-discrimination protection, LGBTI organisations cannot register, media rules still stigmatise homosexuality, and stakeholder reporting documents discrimination/harassment in healthcare and employment. Border document practice and trans-specific violence are explicitly unresolved, so absence is not safety. Combined city-state regime is tolerant in social practice but thin in operative protection, sitting a step below acceptance-plus-working-protections jurisdictions.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No sourced account of immigration treatment of mismatched documents/presentation.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No documented acceptance or rejection of foreign markers.
entry_documents.interaction: Unresolved query is lighter than a known exposure; foreign passport normally does not use domestic surgery-gated recognition.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Section 294 public obscenity up to 3 months exists; soliciting cases cited are 1990-1994 only. No trans-specific arrest, search or custody practice documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Prison service reported 10 trans inmates in 2023 with no recorded assaults; small, dated datum, not a placement protocol.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Latent public-order statute is tangential without documented use against trans visitors.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No bathroom or facility ban documented. Gender-neutral toilets at two university colleges; one temporary conference conversion drew boycott threat/petitions.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Gender-neutral provision exists in limited venues and Pride organisers frame it as complementary, not replacement.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Backlash shows social friction, not a state-imposed universal facility exclusion.

care_services.exposure: 2025 stakeholder report cites discrimination and harassment in healthcare for trans residents; no visitor-specific denial documented.
care_services.protection: Health minister 2020 stated doctors should respect preferences including sexual orientation; medical council complaint route, none received from self-declared LGBTQ patients in prior 3 years.
care_services.interaction: Resident healthcare friction may reach a care-seeking visitor, but no operative denial or remedy outcome is documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Media regulator limits promotion of homosexual lifestyle; 2025 broadcast code grouped homosexuality with paedophilia/incest, prompting review calls. No trans-specific expression crime documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Same-sex conduct decriminalised 2022; Pride held annually since 2009 with ~28,000 recent crowds; bars/clubs operate.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Stigmatising media framing is secondary sexuality framing, not documented trans-targeted enforcement.

minors_guardians.exposure: No visitor/minor rule documented. No recognised same-sex relationship, no spousal standing for a relationship read as same-sex under birth-sex status.
minors_guardians.interaction: Resident adoption/marriage gaps do not create a documented Traveller-facing minor exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence data located to compare with general homicide; no documented police targeting of trans visitors.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Community reported feeling safer after repeal in 2023; youth survey 2021 showed 80% willing to work with LGBTQ people.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Documented social acceptance outweighs silence on violence, but silence is not evidence of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Workplace fairness law effective Jan 2025 does not cover gender identity/expression; LGBTI organisations cannot register, limiting formal recourse infrastructure.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Medical council complaints exist in principle; no operative gender-identity remedy documented.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin formal recourse plus unresolved border practice holds score below protections-with-remedies tier, not to severe-risk tier.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in that no criminalisation and relatively respectful practice, but 0.75-C documents accepted matching passports, trained officers and a tribunal with compensation. Here border practice is undocumented and no gender-identity remedy is documented, so lower.

0.65-B has documented care refusal but a working ombudsperson who reversed it within hours. Here healthcare discrimination is reported for residents without a documented working reversal, while no visitor detention or exclusion is documented, so similar-to-slightly higher.

0.85-A combines explicit gender-identity equality law, chosen-name documents, independent oversight and discipline. This jurisdiction lacks gender-identity protection, bars LGBTI registration and retains stigmatising media rules, so materially lower despite Pride and decriminalisation.

parsed.synthesis: Combined operative regime: no documented universal-exposure measure, organised targeting, or custodial harm; social practice shows Pride, bars and reported post-repeal safety. The operative negatives are thin protection (no GI ground, unregistrable organisations, stigmatising broadcast rules) and explicitly unknown border/violence practice. That combination is documented acceptance without working protections - a step below the 0.75-0.85 tier, well above jurisdictions with enforced targeting or imprisonment.
